memory_candidates.content: When reconciling a namespace-divergence residue by hand-editing a JSON index, re-measure the live data before acting even when a prior report already enumerated the residue -- the strict-.id-only count (32 FTS-only / 17 index-only) and the bridged/deduplicated count used for actual remediation (17 unpaired needing a new entry, 15 already-bridged needing no action, 1 recorded exception) are BOTH correct but answer different questions. Conflating them either causes wasted work (adding parent entries for ids that already resolve via a path-derived bridge) or missed work (skipping ids that genuinely lack any index coverage). Reconcile by classifying each strict-divergence id: does its bare-directory FTS key already resolve via SOME other index entry's path? If yes, no action; if no, it needs a new entry.

A newly-created script cited by name inside a skill/SKILL.md (e.g. a `literature-doc-key.sh` sourced anchor) is not automatically deployed -- deploy manifests (manifest.json's `scripts` list) require explicit per-file registration, and a missing entry produces no error at deploy time, only a silent runtime no-op (e.g. `[ -x "$SCRIPT" ]` guards failing closed and skipping a whole check). When a phase adds a new script file that another phase's logic depends on at runtime, verify its presence in the deployed tree by diffing source-store vs. deployed paths (not just checking the source store), and grep the manifest's file list for the new filename -- do not assume a file existing in the source store means it reached the deployed tree.

When escalating a WARN-only check to a hard failure gated on a known-exceptions list, verify the gate variable itself fires true/false by execution against both the clean case and a known-bad fixture -- do not rely on an existing test that only checks the raw (pre-classification) bucket membership, since a new classification layer added on top of that bucket could silently swallow the case the old test still 'passes' against. Building a minimal standalone fixture and directly inspecting the new gate variable (not just the report text) caught this distinction here.
